title: ChatCompletions Interop Reformulator for Legacy Client Semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tolerant, observable reformulation layer that maps Redwood's native chat request/response model to the OpenAI Chat Completions (CC) semantics expected by legacy clients. This ticket focuses on correctness and fidelity for streaming boundaries, function/tool call signaling, and structured output envelopes while preserving Redwood runtime guarantees (idempotency, backpressure, and partial-response telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: Requests from legacy CC-style clients are accepted and mapped to Redwood canonical request shape with no loss of tool call intent or structured output metadata.
Streaming token frames sent to clients use SSE/HTTP2 framing compatible with major OpenAI client libraries and include clear start/finish markers for function calls.
Function/tool calling lifecycle is represented idempotently: tool invocation, tool output, and model resumption are replayable and unambiguous across retries.
Structured outputs (JSON blobs, JSONL, and typed candidates) are preserved or transformed into an OA-compatible delta stream without corrupting the KV-cache replay semantics.
Metrics for per-request latency, token counts, tool-invocations, and failed-mapping events are emitted to the console telemetry pipeline.
Automated end-to-end tests cover: streaming partials, tool-call roundtrip, malformed client payloads, and client-initiated reconnects.
notes: Privacy: layer must not cache customer tool outputs in public cache buckets; follow private KV config for Dedicated/Private deployments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Request normalizer - map legacy 'messages' + 'functions' schema into Redwood canonical schema; add validation and warning headers for unsupported fields.
Phase 2: Streaming mapper - implement token/event envelope translator that converts Redwood streaming events into CC delta frames; include heartbeat and reconnect hints.
Phase 3: Function call lifecycle - implement explicit tool-call events: call.start, call.output, call.end; ensure idempotent call IDs and replay safety.
Phase 4: Structured output fidelity - add JSON-safe delta merger and fallback to full-response emission on recovery.
Phase 5: Observability and QA - instrument counters, SLO dashboards, and run regression suite against canonical OA fixtures.
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Spike completed to evaluate existing cc-proxy framing code; found mismatches in tool-call boundary semantics (notes attached).
2025-02-25: Implemented request normalizer prototype; wire up basic field mapping and validation. Demoed to PM/Design — feedback: preserve 'role' and custom metadata headers.

2025-02-28: Streaming mapper v0 pushed to feature branch; passes internal fuzzer for out-of-order fragments but not yet resilient to client reconnects. Opened GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428

2025-03-03: Design review with UX and PM — agreed to emit explicit 'tool_call' start/end markers in SSE and to attach canonical 'call_id' for traceability. Added telemetry counters for 'mapping_error' and 'call_retries'.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): Ensure the mapping layer surfaces a clear deprecation path for legacy fields so we can signal clients to migrate.
Design (Maya Chen): Streaming UX should prefer incremental JSON patches for structured outputs; fallback to 'final' when patch reconstruction fails.
SRE (Diego Ramos): Confirm that streaming backpressure honours tenant-level rate limits and does not cause unbounded memory growth on reconnect.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misinterpreting function-call boundaries may cause duplicate tool invocations. Mitigation: allocate deterministic call IDs and provide at-least-once semantics with dedupe on backend tool adapters.
Risk: Legacy clients expect immediate newline-delimited JSON vs SSE frames. Mitigation: support both framing modes behind a negotiation header 'X-Client-Frame' and autodetect common client libs.
Risk: High cardinality telemetry from malformed payloads. Mitigation: sample mapping_error events and redact sensitive fields before emission.
testing_plan: Unit tests for request field mappings and edge cases (max tokens, missing 'role').
Integration: replay recorded OA fixtures across reconnection scenarios.
Chaos: simulate partial network disconnects at token granularity and assert no duplicate tool calls.
Performance: ensure mapping layer adds <2ms median overhead at 99th percentile under p95 token throughput.
